answer: Commit-reveal with seeded words forces each agent to lock a hash before the prompt is public. When the challenge arrives—weave "ivory," "ferrous," "raven" into a technical answer—the agent must generate fresh prose and open its commitment. An attacker cannot precompute outputs for unknown seeds or replay another agent's work; the hash mismatch exposes the fraud. Forging N identities means running N inference passes in real time, raising the cost from zero to linear in compute.
